Definition: to slaughter an animal (usually in sacrifice)
BiblicalUsage: Zabach is to slaughter an animal, usually in sacrifice, and it runs through the whole story of worship. In Genesis 31:54 Jacob "offered sacrifice upon the mount" and shared a meal with his brethren. Exodus 3:18 sends Moses to Pharaoh to ask that Israel may go "sacrifice to the LORD our God," and Leviticus 9:4 sets out peace offerings "to sacrifice before the LORD." Even Balak sacrifices in Numbers 22:40, offering oxen and sheep to win Balaam's help.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sacrifice is the shape of worship before Christ, and every animal on those altars was pointing forward. I hold that Jacob's meal on the mountain in Genesis 31:54 shows sacrifice was never only about death, it was about fellowship with God, and that the sacrifices Israel offered only made sense because a greater sacrifice was coming. My position is that zabach teaches me worship costs something, and God himself paid the cost.
